cohort: The study included 241 pregnant people diagnosed with anorexia nervosa and 6,418,236 people without an eating disorder diagnosis, all of whom had live-born singleton deliveries in California between 2007 and 2021.
finding: Anorexia nervosa diagnosis during pregnancy was associated with increased likelihood of anemia, preterm labor, oligohydramnios, severe maternal morbidity, small for gestational age or low-birthweight infants, and preterm birth between 32 and 36 weeks with spontaneous preterm labor, with a substantial portion of this excess risk mediated by underweight prepregnancy BMI and inadequate gestational weight gain.
